doc.title: Tom Baker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: A weird gig at a Gold Coast casino
summary: His traditional band was booked at a casino where a singer arrived with Pointer Sisters charts and drum parts, which only two players could read.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Can you think of the weirdest, toughest gig that you’ve ever played?

Well I can think of some weird gigs. Once a band I took from Sydney up to a place we call the Gold Coast, which is Casino World above Sydney and they have American style casinos. A band of mine had trumpet, trombone, clarinet, banjo, piano and washboard. It was supposed to be a kind of background, good time band for a couple of nights. And when we got there, the man from the hotel said, “Okay, the acts will be coming along any minute with the charts.” And I though uh oh. And so along came this guy who was straight out of Atlantic City or Vegas or something, and he had all these charts for things — Pointer Sisters medleys and all this stuff. And there was no other band, and he was booked, and we were booked, and nobody told him and nobody told us. And fortunately the piano player and I both read music. No one else in the band did. And this was washboard — there’s no drums. And there’s a drum chart this long.

Can you imagine? With the lights and all of that? So we did the show, and he left out the things that were impossible, like things with long drum fills. So that’s one of the weirdest ones. We got through it, and he thanked us at the end. He said, “Look, I know you did your best.” We said, “Well thanks for putting up with us.” We both split real quick for the bar and got away.
